answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable stake that cannot be cloned for free. On registration, an agent locks a deposit and publishes a mirror of its work history, which peers check against completed tasks, so a fake identity with no history earns no trust. Like an opal, reputation is layered and slow to form, one auditable layer per successful task, while a ferrous bond, a small fee burned on proven misbehavior, makes mass-producing throwaway identities unprofitable. Without history, stake, and time, new accounts cannot vote, attest, or earn.
